author: Jonathan Ketz
title: Missouri redistricting could happen again in '27, secretary of state says - NewsBreak
text:
By Jonathan Ketz ,
1 hours ago
KANSAS CITY, Mo. — Democratic Congressman Emanuel Cleaver II is calling on Republican Secretary of State Denny Hoskins to certify the signatures that would trigger a vote on new congressional maps.
The statement comes a day after the Missouri Supreme Court ruled the map that gives Republicans the advantage this November can stay in place, at least for now. Wednesday, Cleaver told FOX4 the ruling came as no surprise.
Three people exposed to hantavirus taken to KU Hospital for observation The group People Not Politicians has been fighting against the redrawn maps since September. They even submitted a petition signed by more than 300,000 Missourians. Cleaver, who could lose his seat depending on his voter base, is waiting on that certification.
“The only concern we have at this point is whether the secretary of state is going to slow walk it,” Cleaver said Wednesday. “We think that they have the signatures right now, but they won’t take it to the court and say, ‘We certify that these signatures’ are valid, and they have successfully complied with the constitution.”
“Well, according to state law, our local election authorities and county clerks have until July 27 in order to verify the signatures,” Hoskins said when asked if he was going to slow walk the process. “Then I have from July 28 through August 4 to certify those signatures, so I’m simply following state law.”
FOX4’s follow-up question for him was whether he could certify the signatures right now.
“My understanding is not all of the local election authorities have verified the signatures that they’ve been given,” Hoskins replied.
Piece of Berlin Wall installed at Union Station for new exhibit If Hoskins certifies these signatures, then the referendum would go on the November 2026 ballot, but the Supreme Court’s recent ruling on the Voting Rights Act may affect the future.
“Well, I could see the exact opposite almost,” Hoskins replied when asked if he thinks there’s a good chance Missouri could have a 7-1 map in the 2026 elections and a 6-2 map in the 2028 elections. “I could see a 7-1 map in 2026 and then congressional redistricting in 2027 to get rid of the racial gerrymander district in CD-1, and I could see Missouri trying for an 8-0 map uh for the 2028 election.”
Hoskins’ deadline to certify the signatures is the same day Missourians are voting in their party primaries for who they want to advance to the November elections.
